_about: DC-9-50 (DC-9-51), from Boeing's copy of the Douglas DC-9 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (June 1984, Rev F 5/84; boeing.com's airport planning page, DC9.pdf, 2023), 2.2 General Airplane Dimensions, Model DC-9-51 (page index 16): side, plan and front views on one sheet, a 1-bit scan on graph paper drawn at 0.90 of the DC-9-32 sheet's scale, rendered at scale 4.44 to about its pixels (47.29 px a meter). Pixels of layers.py --mode image rasters, --unrotate, line centres: the side --rotate 179.74 (drawn a quarter of a degree off level), the plan and front --rotate 180. Clips (stored page points): side 72,317,525,412; plan 82,397,525,700; front 147,147,457,252. Scaled by the printed 36.96 m (121 ft 3 in) from the nose to the tail cone (17, 1765 px). The DC-9-30's placed points (dc93/) moved by its two plugs (plug.py: 2.35 m at 12 m, ahead of the wing, and 2.00 m at 21 m, behind it; from the two sheets' printed 18.57 m and 16.22 m nose to main gear and 36.96 m and 32.61 m nose to tail cone), the side view 0.99 of the DC-9-32's height (this sheet draws the tube 3.52 m tall), then snapped. The nose's crown above the windshield, the belly past the nose gear and the JT8D-17 nacelle (its later thrust reverser: the cowl ends at 1540 px, the reverser's outline inside it isn't the nacelle's) placed here; the wing's tip and the tailplane's leading edge re-placed here. The front view's points from the DC-9-30's, moved to this sheet's fuselage, then snapped. Windows: the sheet's 44 solid ones (a dashed one at the aft end left out), their height and width the MD-80's. Doors: the main entry door (left), the two overwing exits and the cargo doors (right, dashed) as drawn; the service door (right) from 2.7.4 (as the DC-9-30's). Cockpit panes: the MD-80's (the same nose). The side view draws the tube 3.52 m tall against the printed 3.61 m (the front view 3.57 m): fit to the printed height. Rebuild: layers.py per view, snap.py, features.py, build.py dc95/recipe.json W, smooth.py, fit_height.py, dc93/straighten.py, windshield.py.

windows.note: Each window's place along the body measured on the DC-9-51 sheet's side view (2.2), which draws them as closed outlines: 44 solid, from just behind the main door to the nacelle's inlet, the overwing exits' windows among them. A dashed window at the aft end (optional on some aircraft) is left out. Their height and width are the MD-80's (MD82: the same cabin section and windows).

sources.title: Boeing (Douglas Aircraft Company), DC-9 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (June 1984, revised F 5/84), 2.2 General Airplane Dimensions: Model DC-9-51 and Model DC-9-32; 2.7.4 Passenger Entrance and Service Door Clearances, Model DC-9
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the DC-9-51 sheet's side, plan and front views (tools/trace/dc95/), starting from the DC-9-30's points (tools/trace/dc93/) with its two plugs added; the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. The sheet is a 1-bit scan on graph paper (about 47 px a meter at the scale rendered, so outlines are good to about 5 cm). Scaled by the printed 36.96 m from the nose to the tail cone. The wing, fin and tailplane are the DC-9-30's, snapped onto this sheet's drawing of them; the JT8D-17 nacelle with its later thrust reverser is this sheet's. Its side view draws the tube 3.52 m tall against the printed 3.61 m (its front view 3.57 m), so the fuselage is fit to the printed height (fit_height.py). The sheet draws 44 cabin windows (a dashed one at the aft end, optional, left out), the main entry door, two overwing exits a side and the cargo doors (dashed); the service door is placed from 2.7.4 as on the DC-9-30. Windows' height and width and the cockpit panes are the MD-80's (MD82: the same nose and cabin section). The nose strakes 2.7.4 notes on the DC-9-51 aren't drawn. Confidence medium: a scan.
